peptide.name: HGH (Somatropin)
peptide.summary: Somatropin is recombinant human growth hormone (rhGH) -- a bioidentical, 191-amino-acid copy of the growth hormone naturally secreted by the anterior pituitary. It is FDA-approved under multiple brand names for a specific list of growth-disorder and deficiency indications, and separately (as Serostim) for HIV-associated wasting. Unlike the GH secretagogues elsewhere in this encyclopedia (e.g., ipamorelin, CJC-1295, GHRP-6), somatropin supplies growth hormone directly rather than stimulating the pituitary to release its own.
peptide.description: Somatropin is produced via recombinant DNA technology (typically in E. coli or mammalian expression systems) and is structurally identical to the major isoform of endogenous human growth hormone: a 191-amino-acid, single-chain polypeptide with four cysteine residues forming two intrachain disulfide bonds. Multiple manufacturers market essentially identical or near-identical rhGH products under different brand names (Genotropin, Humatrope, Norditropin, Saizen, Nutropin, Omnitrope, Zomacton), with Serostim licensed specifically for HIV-associated wasting. It binds the growth hormone receptor (GHR), a class I cytokine receptor that dimerizes upon ligand binding and activates JAK2-STAT5 intracellular signaling, driving hepatic IGF-1 production and direct anabolic and metabolic effects across multiple tissues. FDA-approved indications include growth hormone deficiency and specific growth disorders in children (idiopathic and organic GHD, Turner syndrome, Prader-Willi syndrome, small for gestational age, Noonan syndrome, SHOX deficiency, chronic renal insufficiency) and growth hormone deficiency in adults (childhood-onset or adult-onset, from pituitary tumors, surgery, radiation, or trauma), plus HIV-associated wasting/cachexia (Serostim). It is a distinct entry from the shorter, injectable GH secretagogue peptides in this encyclopedia -- somatropin is the hormone itself, not a stimulator of its release, and it is a fully approved prescription drug with an extensive body of clinical evidence, unlike the research-chemical secretagogues.
peptide.mechanism_of_action: Binds the growth hormone receptor (GHR), a class I cytokine receptor, causing receptor dimerization and activation of JAK2-STAT5 intracellular signaling. This drives hepatic and peripheral IGF-1 production and directly promotes protein synthesis, lipolysis, and tissue growth. Effects include increased linear growth in children, and in adults a shift in body composition toward more lean mass and less fat mass, along with effects on bone density and lipid metabolism; supraphysiologic doses can raise blood glucose, cause fluid retention, and cause joint pain.
peptide.sequence: 191-amino-acid single-chain polypeptide, identical to pituitary-derived human growth hormone (4 cysteine residues, 2 intrachain disulfide bonds)

half_life.note: Subcutaneous rhGH has a relatively short circulating half-life (on the order of a few hours), but its downstream effect is mediated through sustained IGF-1 elevation rather than direct GH persistence; dosing is typically once daily.

peptide.evidence_note: Extensive decades-long clinical evidence base supporting FDA-approved indications (pediatric growth disorders, adult GHD, HIV-associated wasting). Off-label use for anti-aging, general athletic performance, or body-composition enhancement in GH-sufficient adults is far more common than approved use but has a substantially thinner and more mixed evidence base, and is not an FDA-approved indication.
peptide.fda_status_note: FDA-approved (under multiple brand names: Genotropin, Humatrope, Norditropin, Omnitrope, Saizen, Nutropin, Zomacton) for growth hormone deficiency and specific growth disorders in children and adults, and (as Serostim) for HIV-associated wasting/cachexia. Off-label use for anti-aging or performance purposes in GH-sufficient individuals is not an approved indication and is prohibited in competitive sport. Prescription-only for all approved uses.
peptide.compounding_note: An FDA-approved biologic drug (multiple branded products). 'Research-grade' or gray-market HGH sold outside a pharmacy/prescription channel is not the approved product and carries unknown purity/dosing risk.

benefits.label: Linear growth in children with GHD/growth disorders
benefits.detail: Well-established efficacy restoring normal growth trajectories in FDA-approved pediatric indications.

benefits.label: Improved body composition in adult GHD
benefits.detail: Shifts body composition toward increased lean mass and decreased fat mass in adults with confirmed growth hormone deficiency.

benefits.label: HIV-associated wasting (Serostim)
benefits.detail: FDA-approved specifically for HIV-associated wasting or cachexia.

benefits.label: General anti-aging / performance use (off-label, thin evidence)
benefits.detail: Widely used off-label in GH-sufficient adults for body composition, recovery, and anti-aging; this use is not FDA-approved and has a much thinner, more mixed evidence base than the approved deficiency indications.

risks.label: Glucose intolerance / insulin resistance
risks.detail: Supraphysiologic dosing raises blood glucose and can worsen insulin sensitivity.

risks.label: Fluid retention / joint pain
risks.detail: Common at higher, particularly off-label/supraphysiologic doses.

risks.label: Theoretical malignancy concern with IGF-1 elevation
risks.detail: Sustained IGF-1 elevation is a theoretical concern for growth-sensitive tissue; monitored in clinical use.

risks.label: Off-label/gray-market product quality
risks.detail: HGH obtained outside an approved pharmacy/prescription channel carries unknown purity, dosing accuracy, and counterfeit risk.

contraindications.label: Active malignancy
contraindications.detail: Growth hormone/IGF-1 stimulation is generally contraindicated in the presence of active tumors.

contraindications.label: Severe obesity with respiratory impairment (specific pediatric contexts, e.g. Prader-Willi)
contraindications.detail: Boxed-warning-level caution in some pediatric populations per FDA labeling.

interactions.effect: GH raises blood glucose; may require adjustment of diabetes medications.
Can attenuate the growth-promoting effect of somatropin; monitor with concurrent use.

reconstitution.note: Supplied as a lyophilized powder (reconstituted with the provided diluent per the specific brand's device/cartridge system) or as a pre-mixed liquid formulation, depending on brand. Reconstitution and storage instructions differ by product; follow the specific brand's prescribing information rather than a generic protocol.

lyophilized.stability: Per each product's specific FDA labeling.

reconstituted.stability: Use within the brand-specific window after reconstitution/first use; varies by product.

peptide.disclaimer: For research and educational purposes only. This is not medical advice. Somatropin is a prescription biologic approved for specific indications; off-label use in GH-sufficient adults is not an approved use and is prohibited in competitive sport. Use only under a licensed healthcare provider.

dose_ranges.context: Adult growth hormone deficiency (approved labeling, typical range)
dose_ranges.note: Approved adult-GHD dosing is individualized and typically starts low, titrated based on IGF-1 levels and clinical response/tolerability per the specific brand's prescribing information. Pediatric dosing is weight-based and differs substantially; follow the specific product's approved labeling.

protocols.name: Adult GHD replacement (per approved labeling, general pattern)
protocols.description: Approved labeling for adult growth hormone deficiency specifies once-daily subcutaneous dosing, started low and titrated upward based on IGF-1 levels, clinical response, and tolerability, under physician supervision. Exact starting doses and titration schedules differ by brand; follow the specific product's prescribing information.
protocols.cycling_notes: Chronic replacement therapy while indication persists; not cycled. Managed by an endocrinologist or prescribing physician.
protocols.disclaimer: Summary of general approved-labeling patterns for educational reference. Not a substitute for a specific product's prescribing information or medical advice.

related.note: Tesamorelin stimulates the pituitary's own GH release via the GHRH receptor, while somatropin supplies growth hormone directly; both affect the same GH/IGF-1 axis through different mechanisms.
Ipamorelin and other GH secretagogues stimulate endogenous GH release, in contrast to somatropin, which is exogenous growth hormone itself.
